title: Asanga and the dog
hookLine: after years of failure, Asanga tends a wounded dog and Maitreya appears (a legend)

cards: A monk sits alone in a cave on a mountain. His name is Asanga, and he has one wish: to see Maitreya, the Buddha who is to come, face to face, and learn from him. He meditates for years.
Nothing. He gives up, walks down the mountain, sees something that shames him into trying again, and climbs back up. Years more.
Nothing. Again and again. At last, Tibetan tellers say, he leaves for good.
On the road down, a dog is lying in the dust.

teach.h: A NEEDLE FROM AN IRON BAR.
teach.b: Each time Asanga quits, he meets a small lesson in patience. A man rubbing an iron bar with a soft cloth, to make a needle. Drops of water that have worn a hollow into stone.
Each sends him back up the mountain, and still nothing.

teach.h: HIS OWN FLESH FOR THE MAGGOTS.
teach.b: On his last walk down he finds the dog, its back half an open wound, crawling with maggots. Something in him breaks open. He wants to help the dog, but he doesn't want to kill the maggots either.

So he cuts flesh from his own thigh to give them somewhere to go, then closes his eyes and bends to lift them away with his tongue, so as not to crush them with his fingers. His tongue touches the ground. The dog is gone.
Maitreya stands there, shining. Asanga, in tears, asks why he never came in all those years.
Maitreya answers that he was always there. What hid him was Asanga's own mind, until great compassion cleared it. To prove it, the story says, Asanga carries Maitreya on his shoulder into the town.

teach.h: ONE OLD WOMAN SEES A DOG.
teach.b: Almost no one sees anything; one old woman sees only a dog. It's a legend, and Tibetan teachers tell it as one, with a point.
Tradition goes on to credit Asanga with teachings received from Maitreya, the ground of the school we meet in two days. But the story's own lesson is simpler. Effort alone didn't let him see.

how: Tibetan Buddhist teachers tell the story of Asanga and the dog when teaching great compassion, and Asanga is honored in Tibetan tradition as a founder of the lineage of vast activity received from Maitreya.

games.q: you're Asanga, leaving the mountain for good. a dog lies in the road, its wound full of maggots. what do you do?
o: step around it; you've given up enough already.
kill the maggots to save the dog.
save the dog without harming the maggots, even at cost to yourself.
games.why: he cuts flesh from his own thigh for the maggots and bends to lift them with his tongue. then the dog is gone, and Maitreya is there.

practice: Bring to mind one hurting thing, a wilted plant, a friend who has gone quiet, a sore muscle in your own back, and give it plain attention first, the way Asanga finally looked at the dog.
Then let one gentle thing you could do for it come to mind, and rest with that wish.

wordCard.voice: Maitreya. The Buddha who is to come, whom Asanga saw at last in the place of a wounded dog he had tended. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit Maitreya: the name of the Buddha who is to come.

carryVoice: Your line: compassion opened his eyes. Years of effort, and the door was a wounded dog. Until tomorrow.
